_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- IMAGER preset: TESS (one of its four identical cameras, modeled as a refractor), with the four-camera array for context
_meta.companion: data/imaging/tess.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows data/imaging/megacam_ztf_small.json / widefield.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; tess: title, preset (machine-readable explorer inputs), recommended_preset (prose), params, performance (validation targets), not_found, conflicts, notes (+ notes_quotes).
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/imaging/tess/. DERIVED = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote except those with check = 'image' / 'image+caption' was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page (PDF page index = 'PDF p.' / slide number), tag-stripped HTML, the .py source as text, and the FITS header split into 80-character cards.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, dashes, minus signs, mu, degree glyphs (ring U+25E6 and the Symbol-font private-use U+F0B0 of the C15/C15S text layers -> degree), multiplication sign (x) normalised; whitespace collapsed; line-end hyphenation joined; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; a quote also passes if it matches with all whitespace removed (flagged nospace).
_meta.frames: x = along a row of chips (2 per row) = across the 24-deg width of the four-camera strip; y = between the two rows = along the 96-deg strip (from the TP camera Euler angles). Gaps are between the active 2048 x 2048 imaging areas.

TP.cite: tess-point (C. J. Burke, A. Levine, M. Fausnaugh, R. Vanderspek et al., MIT), tess_stars2px.py VERSION 0.9.5, GitHub tessgi/tess-point commit 1bcd929d2c02042297ecb1b6299b3d95953c2c9b (2026-09-10). Its hard-coded focal-plane geometry ('from rfpg5_c1kb.txt') is the MIT POC analytic model of TESS Instrument Handbook Sec. 9.3.1, fitted in flight to bright-star positions: per camera a focal length, a radial polynomial in tan(theta) (distortion) and the position and rotation of each CCD. The file itself warns the hard-coded geometry 'is not up to date' (pixel-level accuracy)

tess.title: TESS camera (one of four identical): seven-element f/1.4 refractive lens, 105 mm entrance pupil, 146 mm focal length, 2 x 2 mosaic of MIT/LL CCID-80 CCDs (2048 x 2048, 15 um); four cameras form the 24 x 96 deg strip

preset.telescope_type: refractor: one TESS camera lens (seven-element f/1.4 hybrid Petzval, two aspheric surfaces) with the four-CCD mosaic at its focus; no mirrors, no central obstruction
preset.field_circle_note: published: 24 x 24 deg unvignetted, 34 deg diagonal (C15). In the explorer's linear plate scale (1412.8"/mm) the mosaic corners sit at 35.02 deg diagonal, so 35.2 deg (2110') just encloses the CCDs; the real (distorted) corners are at 33.3 deg

chip.model: MIT/LL CCID-80 (frame transfer; frame-store area masked, excluded here)

gap_within_row.basis: DERIVED: mean of the 8 within-row gaps of the four cameras in the in-flight focal-plane geometry (TP)

gap_between_rows.basis: DERIVED: mean of the 8 between-row gaps (TP)

preset.axes: x = along a row of 2 chips = across the 24-deg width of the four-camera strip; y = between the 2 rows = along the 96-deg strip (DERIVED from the TP camera Euler angles). The optical axis falls in the cross-shaped gap at the centre of the mosaic.

distortion.model: radial: r = f tan(theta) (c1 + c2 tan^2 + c3 tan^4 + c4 tan^6 + c5 tan^8), fitted in flight (TP); pincushion relative to the distortion-free (gnomonic) mapping
distortion.check: SPOC WCS of Sector 1 camera 1 CCD 1 at its reference pixel (~CCD centre, 8.9 deg off axis): 20.54-20.55"/px; TP model there 20.57"/px (geometric mean of 20.32 radial and 20.82 tangential)

psf.published_ee: 50% within 15 x 15 um (1 px), 90% within 60 x 60 um (4 x 4 px) (R15 Table 1); predicted on orbit in one 15 um pixel: 55% at (0,0), 23% at (11,0), 18% at (11,11) deg (P16)
psf.note: aberration-limited; diffraction (1.22 lambda/D = 1.9" at 786.5 nm) is negligible against 21" pixels, so psf 'diff' would make the image far too sharp. The PSF grows from compact on axis to chevrons beyond ~6 deg (IH 7.6)

array.camera_gap_arcmin: < 10 along the camera centrelines, ~10' more at the corners (distortion)

preset.flags: F = 146/105 DERIVED (published f/1.4); gaps DERIVED from the in-flight geometry fit (published: ~1.5 mm, 2 mm, 63.482 mm array); distortion DERIVED from the fitted radial polynomial; field circle chosen for the linear model

tess.recommended_preset: Refractor, direct. D = 0.105 m (entrance pupil, R15 'entrance pupil diameter of 10.5 cm'), eps = 0 (all-refractive), F = 1.3905 DERIVED = 146 mm / 105 mm (published f/1.4; 146 mm from IH Table 2.1 and C15S), f = 146.0 mm; in flight the four cameras fit 145.95-146.04 mm (TP). Field: 24 x 24 deg unvignetted (34 deg diagonal); field circle 35.2 deg (2110') so the linear model's mosaic corners (35.02 deg) fit. Band I (TESS 600-1000 nm, centred on I_C 786.5 nm). Detector: 4 x CCID-80, 2048 x 2048 imaging pixels of 15 um (frame stores excluded), rows [2, 2] centred; gaps DERIVED from the in-flight CCD positions: 1.74 mm (116 px, 40.9') between the two chips of a row, 1.58 mm (106 px, 37.3') between the rows (published: ~1.5 mm IH, 2 mm R15, 36'-41' on sky IH). Validate: 21.19"/px on axis (published 21" = 0.35'); 4 x 2048^2 = 16,777,216 px; field 24 x 24 deg nominal (explorer will give 24.79 x 24.73 deg and 581 deg^2 because it has no distortion; true 24.17 x 24.09 deg and 538 deg^2); PSF 50% EE in 1 px, 90% in 4 x 4 px. Distortion: pincushion, radial scale 21.20 -> 17.86"/px at the corners (-16%), pixel solid angle -21% (DERIVED from TP; WCS-checked). Four cameras: 1 x 4 strip, 24 x 96 deg = 2300 deg^2, boresights at +-12 and +-36 deg.

distortion.derived: DERIVED from the camera-1 fit (cameras 2-4 within 0.2%), with 15 um pixels: on axis 21.20"/px both ways; at the edge midpoint (r = 31.5 mm, theta = 12.04 deg) radial 19.55"/px, tangential 20.49"/px, pixel solid angle 400.6 arcsec^2 (-10.9%); at the corner (r = 44.6 mm, theta = 16.59 deg) radial 17.86"/px (-15.8%), tangential 19.81"/px (-6.5%), solid angle 353.8 arcsec^2 (-21.3%). A distortion-free (gnomonic, r = f tan theta) lens would lose only cos^2 theta = 8.2% radially and cos theta = 4.2% tangentially at 16.6 deg; the distortion adds a further 8.3% (radial) and 2.5% (tangential). r / (f tan theta) - 1 = sum of the c_i terms - 1 = +0.12% at 3.9 deg, +0.46% at 7.8 deg, +1.17% at 12.0 deg, +2.56% at 16.6 deg.

not_found: A published distortion amplitude (in % or arcsec/px across the field): only the qualitative IH Sec. 8.1 statement (~10' larger camera spacing at the corners 'due to the distortion of the lenses') and the fitted coefficients in TP; all distortion numbers here are DERIVED from TP and cross-checked against one SPOC WCS.
A pixel scale published to better than 21" (0.35'); 21.19"/px is DERIVED from the 146 mm focal length.
As-built CCD gaps in mm from the hardware papers: only '~1.5 mm' (IH), '2 mm' (R15, HEA) and the 63.482 mm array requirement (P16); the preset gaps are DERIVED from the in-flight geometry fit (TP).
The lens prescription (radii, glasses, thicknesses, stop position): only element count, asphere surfaces, tolerances and the Fig. 2 drawing (C15).

Woods et al. 2016 (SPIE 9904, 'The TESS camera: modeling and measurements with deep depletion devices'), Krishnamurthy et al. 2016/2019, Balonek et al. 2017 and Wellman et al. 2019 (SPIE) were not obtained (publisher paywall; no open copy found).
A published active (gaps-excluded) solid angle per camera; 538 deg^2 (TP) and 581.4 deg^2 (linear) are DERIVED.
conflicts: CCD gap: 2 mm (R15, HEA) vs ~1.5 mm (IH Sec. 4.2) vs 2.042 mm implied by the 63.482 mm array requirement (P16) vs in flight 1.72-1.76 mm within rows and 1.54-1.64 mm between rows (TP, DERIVED). On sky: 36'-41' (IH) = 1.53-1.74 mm at 1412.8"/mm, matching TP.
Array size: 62 x 62 mm (R15, IH Sec. 4.2) vs 63 x 63 mm (IH Sec. 2.3.1) vs 63.482 mm (P16) vs 63.2 x 63.0-63.1 mm (TP). 62 mm cannot hold two 30.72 mm chips plus a 2 mm gap (63.44 mm).
Bandpass red end: 1000 nm (R15, C15, HEA, IH Fig. 3.3) vs 1040 nm (IH Table 2.1). Filter blocking edge: 530 nm (C15), cut-on ~600 nm (R15, IH).
Focal ratio: f/1.4 (all) vs 146 / 105 = 1.3905 (DERIVED); the published f/# is rounded.
Combined field: 2300 deg^2 (R15) vs '3200 deg^2' (HEAT image; 24 x 96 = 2304). Field of regard '48x 48' (C15, a 2 x 2 arrangement) vs the flown 24 x 96 strip (R15, IH, TP).
PSF: R15 Table 1 '50% within 15 x 15 um (one pixel)' vs R15 Sec. 4.1 '50% ensquared-energy half-width is 15 um' (a 30 x 30 um box if read literally); HEA repeats the half-width wording.
Frame-store format: 2048 x 2048 (R15, HEA) vs 2048 x 2068 (IH). Not used by the preset.
Entrance pupil off axis: IH text says it 'falls off as cos(theta)' (100.4 mm at 17 deg) but IH Fig. 3.2 shows ~102.6 mm at ~17 deg.
C15 Sec. 1 'frame size of 2k x 2k pixels' vs '4k x 4k pixels' (C15 Fig. 2, C15S, R15 4096 x 4096): a slip.
notes: Model: a refractor (objective lens, detector at its focus, direct). D = 105 mm, F = 1.3905, f = 146.0 mm, eps = 0. The real lens is a 7-element f/1.4 hybrid Petzval 211 mm long (C15S), its aperture stop behind the oversized first element (C15 Fig. 2), so the whole 24 x 24 deg field is unvignetted (IH 3.1.1).

The explorer's linear plate scale is exact only on axis. TESS has strong pincushion distortion relative to a gnomonic mapping: the radial pixel scale falls from 21.20"/px on axis to 19.55" at the edge midpoints and 17.86" at the corners, the tangential scale to 20.49" and 19.81"; a corner pixel sees 21% less sky. Consequences for validation: the explorer will report a field 24.79 x 24.73 deg (true 24.17 x 24.09) and 581 deg^2 of CCD (true 538).

Mosaic: 2 rows of 2 CCID-80 chips (2048 x 2048 imaging px, 15 um; frame-store halves masked), rows centred. The larger gap (1.74 mm) separates the two chips within a row, the smaller (1.58 mm) the two rows; the optical axis lies in the central cross of the gaps.

Four cameras: boresights at -36, -12, +12, +36 deg from the spacecraft +Z axis along one line, fields nearly abutting (< 10' on the centreline), forming the 24 x 96 deg sector strip; the strip's long axis runs along the focal-plane y axis (between rows).

PSF: aberration-limited, not diffraction-limited (lambda/D = 1.5" vs 21" pixels). Published: 50% of the energy in one pixel and 90% in 4 x 4 px (design, FOV average); predicted on orbit 55% in one pixel on axis, 23% at 11 deg, 18% at the (11, 11) deg corner direction (P16); in flight the peak pixel holds 0.2-0.4 of a star's light (IH). A Gaussian matching '50% in one pixel' has FWHM 1.12 px = 23.7" (DERIVED).

Collecting area: pi/4 x 10.5^2 = 86.59 cm^2; IH Sec. 3.1.2 quotes 'an effective area of 86.6 cm2 on axis and a drop of 4.5% in the furthest corner of the FOV' (the first number is the geometric pupil area).
